name_note: The GTDB species also contains genomes that NCBI names Micrococcus yunnanensis and Micrococcus aloeverae, so it is broader than Micrococcus luteus as used in papers.

sentences.text: Micrococcus luteus is a gram-positive, coagulase-negative coccus commonly regarded as a non-pathogenic commensal organism of human skin.
Within the skin microbiome, described as a diverse community that plays a crucial role in maintaining skin health, this bacterium is reported to exhibit potential for promoting skin health.
It is frequently considered a contaminant when isolated in blood cultures, but a case report of septic shock argues it may act as an opportunistic pathogen in certain clinical settings.
A skin isolate was unique among skin isolates tested in negating Staphylococcus aureus-induced IL-33 and TSLP release from keratinocytes, through a serine protease called PA domain protein.
Culture filtrate of a strain isolated from human skin, tested on human keratinocytes and fibroblasts, enhanced expression of genes involved in skin hydration, barrier function and cell proliferation.
